---
title: "6. Plots"
engine: pari-gp
format: html
---

A cell whose output is an SVG document becomes a figure. gp has three
functions that return SVG — `plothexport`, `plothrawexport` and
`plotexport` — and all three work, because the engine looks at the output
rather than at the name of the function.

## A function of one variable

```{gp}
#| label: fig-sine
#| fig-cap: "$\\sin x$ on $[-2\\pi, 2\\pi]$"
#| fig-alt: "Two full periods of a sine wave"
plothexport("svg", X = -2*Pi, 2*Pi, sin(X))
```

@fig-sine is a real cross-reference, because the cell has a `label` starting
with `fig-`.

## Something worth plotting

The modulus of $\zeta$ on the critical line, with the first few zeros
visible as the points where it touches the axis:

```{gp}
#| label: fig-zeta
#| fig-cap: "$|\\zeta(1/2 + it)|$ for $0 \\le t \\le 40$"
#| fig-alt: "A wavy curve touching zero six times"
plothexport("svg", T = 0.1, 40, abs(zeta(1/2 + I*T)))
```

Six touchdowns, matching the six zeros [computed earlier](05-zeta.qmd).

## Several curves at once

Give `plothexport` a vector and it draws each component:

```{gp}
#| label: fig-bessel
#| fig-cap: "The Bessel functions $J_0$, $J_1$ and $J_2$"
#| fig-alt: "Three decaying oscillations, each starting at a different height"
plothexport("svg", X = 0.01, 20, [besselj(0, X), besselj(1, X), besselj(2, X)])
```

## Scattered points

`plothrawexport` takes two vectors and plots one against the other, without
sampling a function. Here the gap to the next prime, for the first 300
primes — the visible bands are the even gaps:

```{gp}
#| label: fig-gaps
#| fig-cap: "Gap to the next prime, for the first 300 primes"
#| fig-alt: "A scatter of points in horizontal bands at even heights"
#| fig-width: 90%
ps = primes(301);
plothrawexport("svg", vector(300, i, ps[i]), vector(300, i, ps[i+1] - ps[i]))
```

`fig-width` is a CSS width, so the figure above is 90% of the text column.

## What is not captured

`ploth`, `plothraw` and `plotdraw` open a window on a screen device, and
`psploth` writes PostScript. None of them returns SVG, so none of them
becomes a figure here — that is a property of gp, not a limitation of the
engine. Export is the thing to reach for.
